To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the covariant current operator is a gauge field and the gauge field is a covariant current.

the covariant current operator for a derivative-coupled scalar field theory in two dimensions can be defined only if one chooses the gauge-fixing parameter xi to be zero, and that the current operator for the theory in question is identical to that of the free theory, in the sense that the expectation value of a current operator in a free-field state is equal to the expectation value of the current operator in the same state for the theory in which the interaction is turned on.

the current operator in the derivative-interaction model can be written as the sum of two parts, one of which depends explicitly on the coupling constants of the theory and the other of which does not; that the latter part can be identified as the Noether current of the underlying symmetry; and that the former part is a gauge transformation of the latter.

the problem of the construction and interpretation of a current operator in a derivative-coulping model in a two-dimensional space-time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current operator in a theory without a gauge principle is not a well-defined physical object, but that the equations of motion for a theory with a derivative coupling do possess solutions which are gauge invariant.
a covariant current exists for the model under consideration and is unique.
the model is not a gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current operator is not unique in the derivative-coupling models and that the current operator of a theory can only be determined after solving the equations of motions.
there is no current operator which is both conserved and independent of the parameter xi.
the problem of the existence and uniqueness of a current operator in two-dimensional field theories is still open.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current operator is not unique in a gauge theory and that the freedom in the definition of the current operator may be exploited to obtain a current that is conserved and covariant.
the construction of the covariant current operator is model dependent and cannot be inferred from the form of the Lagrangian alone.
the current operator in the derivative-coupling models is not uniquely determined by the equations of motion.
